assumptions: has_fk_to 'users' matches orders.user_id, sessions.user_id, support_tickets.user_id, user_address.user_id
has_field 'created_at' matches the 17 tables that declare created_at (checked by grep of workspace/table)
delete_user_account (called via DELETE /account) is the account-deletion path; its db.bulk.delete on user_address and sessions and db.del on users count toward coverage
purge_expired_sessions is active (schedule has no end date) and is the only task with a delete statement
A rule with no tags on tables is acceptable: the customer did not want to add tags at this stage
Predicted findings (not evaluated; evaluate is forbidden here): rule 1 -> support_tickets, orders; rule 2 -> 16 tables (all created_at tables except sessions)
confusions: RET-002 (template) takes tags: [retained], but nothing is tagged in this workspace, so the template would pass vacuously. Nothing in the skill warns that a template over an untagged workspace reports nothing; I could not tell whether that is intended.

The GDPR recipe says to tag tables (personal, retained) and the erasure function (erasure) first, but the brief forbids changing the workspace and tag changes are the owner's call. I had to build the policy without tags, and the recipe's erasure rule (tags on the function) is not reproducible without them.

table.coverage_required: 'Scope selects the tables; referenced_by selects the covering objects' and 'reaches a table through called functions'. It is not clear whether referenced_by.statements requires the covering object to delete from that table in the same statement, or just any reference; I assumed the statement must aim at the table as its primary table.

has_field matches the exact schema field name only; no way to select 'any table with a timestamp', so created_at is my proxy for personal/customer data and it also catches tables like orgs, tenants, audit_log.

No check reads retention age, and the skill's own 'What no check can see' section says so, but the recipe wording ('Erase and expire personal data') suggests a retention policy is achievable; the customer will read the policy name as more than it is.

The template table lists RET-002 fill as tags only, with no way to scope coverage to tables without tags; the fallback to has_field / has_fk_to is only mentioned in the parameter description, not in the recipe.

The brief says to use `xano policy parse` to find workspace names, but parse output did not flag any unknown names (no warnings shown in text or json output) even though I did not try a deliberately wrong name, so I cannot confirm how strict the name check is.
wished_for: A recipe variant for 'no tags yet' showing has_fk_to / has_field selectors for account-deletion and retention coverage.
A check or param that reads a retention window from task queries, or at least a convention for declaring max age on a table (for example a table-level attribute), so the 2-year limit is checkable.
A coverage param to exempt named tables (for example invoices kept for tax), like except_tags on other checks.
A way to say 'table holds data about a user' without listing tables (a user-link selector across has_fk_to chains, e.g. customers via org).
Guidance on whether a policy that passes over an empty tag set is a finding, a pass, or a warning.
why_confidence: The policy checks that tables tied to users have a delete function and that timestamped tables have a cleanup task. It cannot check the 2-year age, cannot exempt legally retained tables, cannot see backups or vendor copies, and misses newsletter and support-ticket personal data. The findings are predictions from reading the workspace; I did not run evaluate because the brief forbids it.
